cause: The alert is firing on a real, long-dormant retro, not on the platform series. Since homelab#3161 (merged 2026-11-02 20:39Z) the rule takes max by (series). The only stale sample is the pre-series oracle stack retro (job retro-session, stack oracle, no series label), whose last success is 2026-08-17 around 10:17Z. With no series label it becomes its own group, and the annotation renders that group as '<none has ever pushed>', which is wrong wording because it pushed eleven weeks ago. Before #3161 the ungrouped max() let the fresh platform push mask it (the #3161 body says so: a fresh platform push must never hide a stale sibling). The platform r10 report landed 2026-11-02 05:35Z, and a platform quiet-week push on 2026-10-31 20:50Z also cleared the alert, which is why it was silent from about Oct 31 to Nov 2. The onset (pending 2026-11-02 20:41Z) therefore matches the rule change, not a new platform failure: the change exposed an oracle stack retro that has produced nothing since 2026-08-17 (last report PR homelab#246, oracle r3, 2026-08-11). Whether that retro should still run is a decision the repo does not answer.

argocd/resources/pushgateway/retro-report.promtool-rules and prometheusrule.yaml:51 → expr is max by (series) with an absent()*0 fallback; annotation renders a label-less group as '<none has ever pushed>'

gh issue view 3140 (homelab, closed) → oracle feedback-triage series ruling; the new series is born suspended

recommendation: Seat decides one of two: (a) if oracle's stack-level retro is retired, delete the stale Pushgateway group job=retro-session,stack=oracle and the alert clears; (b) if it should run, re-fire it with argo -n agent-coordinator submit --from cronworkflow/<oracle retro>. Separately, correct the '<none has ever pushed>' fallback so a label-less stale group reads as a stale push (argocd/resources/pushgateway/prometheusrule.yaml plus the retro-report.promtool-rules copy, re-synced). No PR from me: clearing the alert depends on the retire-or-run decision.
